sections.heading: 2. Convert SEC and Powered-Land Signals into Evidence-Backed Mandates
paragraphs: Implement sec_edgar_8k_vendor_trigger_arbitrage as a research queue, not a claim that a filing proves seller intent. Monitor SEC EDGAR current-filings feeds and submissions JSON, deduplicating by accession number and extracting Form 8-K Items 5.02, 1.01, and 2.01 plus Form D filings. Executive departures can expose succession needs; material agreements can identify strategic buyers; completed acquisitions can suggest follow-on divestitures. Form D reports an exempt offering, not an SEC endorsement or proof that the stated offering amount was collected. Separate total offering amount from reported sales and read amendments before drafting outreach. Target a reviewed message within sixty minutes of detection during staffed hours; filing latency and feed delays remain outside that promise. For planning, screen 200 filings monthly, identify twenty relevant companies, secure four substantive conversations, and develop one mandate. At a hypothetical twenty-percent eventual close rate, that mandate contributes $5,500 expected retained commission before acquisition cost and timing effects. These are test assumptions, not additional scorecard revenue. Preserve the accession, source excerpt, timestamp, reviewer decision, and business-specific outreach rationale so a second operator can explain exactly why the company entered the pipeline.

Use a shared token bucket capped at five requests per second across all SEC workers, identify the application with a descriptive User-Agent and contact address, cache responses, and honor access errors with backoff. During outages, mirror available SEC nightly bulk ZIP archives for historical lookbacks, including submissions.zip where suitable, and use daily indexes plus archived filings for document coverage the bulk dataset does not provide. Historical replay must never generate fresh-looking duplicate outreach. Create an outreach task keyed by accession, company, and play; require a human to confirm relevance before sending. Allocate, illustratively, $600 research labor, $150 data handling, and $250 specialist review to the monthly experiment: $1,000 divided by one expected mandate equals $1,000 acquisition cost, while five such mandates per expected closing imply $5,000 acquisition cost per closing. If the assumed conversion fails, narrow the event taxonomy rather than increasing message volume blindly. Apply CAN-SPAM requirements under 15 U.S.C. 7704 to commercial email, including accurate routing information and a functioning opt-out. Do not sell securities introductions merely because the research originated in EDGAR; compensation and transaction structure still determine the applicable intermediary requirements.

Implement ferc_grid_interconnection_queue_land_speculation through a separately tracked site thesis. Overlay public ISO or RTO queue records with county parcels, zoning, flood exposure, access rights, substation locations, and utility correspondence using QGIS and dated source layers. A generation interconnection queue entry does not establish deliverable load service for a data center, and distance to a substation does not establish capacity. Require utility-specific service studies, upgrade allocation, easements, milestones, and a credible schedule before representing power availability. An illustrative screen examines forty parcels, advances eight desktop candidates, and commissions two $2,000 specialist reviews plus $1,000 mapping work: $5,000 total research expenditure. A client might separately risk a $10,000 contingent option deposit on one site; that principal never becomes brokerage revenue. The brokerage can target one $27,500 retained commission if the contingent transaction closes, but must carry the full $5,000 research loss if both sites fail. For the option-flipping variant, isolate proprietary option gains from this commission-only scorecard. Let contingent options lapse or reposition land for independently viable uses when service cannot be substantiated, without describing speculative queue proximity as secured power.

sections.heading: 3. Build a Six-Module Ledger with Serialized State Changes and Replay-Safe Posting
paragraphs: Use the reference below as a small, explicit execution core rather than pretending a CRM is an accounting system. Concatenate the six code cells, in displayed order, into broker_ledger.py and run it with Python 3.9 or later; the final module executes an isolated self-test. The code uses only the standard library and creates its test database inside a temporary directory. Production deployment initializes a local SQLite database once, then gives every worker its own connection. BEGIN IMMEDIATE serializes write transactions before reads that decide state changes; the version check rejects stale commands instead of overwriting intervening work. A unique command key plus a canonical request digest makes identical replays return the original result and rejects altered replays. Unique bank references prevent one settlement from paying two invoices. This concurrency model requires a supported local filesystem, not a shared network drive, and all application writers must use these functions. Database administrators remain trusted. Run schema changes through one controlled migration process, restrict database file permissions, and keep encrypted backups. SQLite locking protects ledger transitions; it does not authenticate an escrow officer or validate a seller's representations without the documented human verification process.

The six modules intentionally separate intake, evidence-based workflow, bank observations, and accounting presentation. Screening points prioritize work but never establish licensing eligibility or asset quality. Intake stores the retained fee in integer cents and refuses a reused source key carrying different facts. Every successful transition appends an immutable event and advances the mandate version within the same transaction. Closing posts a debit to commission receivables and a credit to retained-commission revenue; payment posts cash against that receivable only after an independently imported settled bank observation matches the exact amount. Each journal record contains equal debit and credit amounts by construction, avoiding a temporary half-posted entry. The reconciliation view shows receivables, cash movement, earned commission, expense, bank movement, unmatched observations, and the signed ledger balance. Expense posting uses the same atomic event and unique bank-reference discipline. Evidence strings should identify immutable document versions or content hashes, not mutable shared-folder labels. Their presence proves that a reviewer supplied a reference, not that software independently verified the underlying document. Keep that responsibility assigned to a named reviewer in the surrounding task system and preserve the review history with the referenced evidence packet.

Keep the supported scope narrow enough to test completely. This reference handles fixed retained fees, full settled receipts, and cash-paid operating expenses; it rejects partial receipts and does not implement refunds, taxes, foreign exchange, fee amendments, or accounting reversals. Route those exceptions to a reviewed extension with new journal events rather than editing posted records. The ledger contains operator cash only, never escrow principal. Bank observations must come from a separately authenticated statement import; granting a user access to that importer is a distinct permission from approving a closing. The included test proves concurrent identical closing commands produce one event, altered replays fail, a bank reference cannot fund duplicate expenses, and ledger totals remain balanced. It also checks that failed posting rolls back its event. Lock contention can still produce a timeout; callers retry the exact same command key after bounded backoff, without changing its payload. No function sends outreach or initiates a transfer, so the transaction boundary contains no external side effect. If those capabilities are added, introduce a transactional outbox and recipient-side deduplication; do not claim that a committed database row alone makes an external email or wire execute exactly once.

Copy-pasteable Python source appended in displayed order
Atomicity rule and explicit concurrency protection mechanism

rows: Module 1: initialize constrained tables and immutable accounting records

import hashlib
import json
import sqlite3
import tempfile
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from contextlib import contextmanager
from pathlib import Path

SCHEMA = """
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS mandates (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    source_key TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    intake_hash TEXT NOT NULL,
    retained_fee_cents INTEGER NOT NULL
        CHECK(typeof(retained_fee_cents) = 'integer'
              AND retained_fee_cents > 0),
    score INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(score BETWEEN 0 AND 100),
    state TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'NEW'
        CHECK(state IN (
            'NEW', 'QUALIFIED', 'VERIFIED', 'MANDATED',
            'ESCROW', 'CLOSED', 'PAID', 'LOST'
        )),
    version INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK(version >= 0)
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS events (
    command_key TEXT PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL,
    mandate_id INTEGER REFERENCES mandates(id),
    request_hash TEXT NOT NULL,
    event_type TEXT NOT NULL,
    evidence_json TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS bank_observations (
    bank_ref TEXT PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL,
    amount_cents INTEGER NOT NULL
        CHECK(typeof(amount_cents) = 'integer' AND amount_cents != 0),
    settled_on TEXT NOT NULL,
    source_digest TEXT NOT NULL
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS journal (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    command_key TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE
        REFERENCES events(command_key),
    debit_account TEXT NOT NULL
        CHECK(debit_account IN ('AR', 'CASH', 'REVENUE', 'EXPENSE')),
    credit_account TEXT NOT NULL
        CHECK(credit_account IN ('AR', 'CASH', 'REVENUE', 'EXPENSE')),
    amount_cents INTEGER NOT NULL
        CHECK(typeof(amount_cents) = 'integer' AND amount_cents > 0),
    bank_ref TEXT UNIQUE REFERENCES bank_observations(bank_ref),
    CHECK(debit_account != credit_account)
);
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS events_no_update
BEFORE UPDATE ON events BEGIN
    SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'events are immutable');
END;
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS events_no_delete
BEFORE DELETE ON events BEGIN
    SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'events are immutable');
END;
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS journal_no_update
BEFORE UPDATE ON journal BEGIN
    SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'journal is immutable');
END;
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS journal_no_delete
BEFORE DELETE ON journal BEGIN
    SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'journal is immutable');
END;
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS bank_no_update
BEFORE UPDATE ON bank_observations BEGIN
    SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'bank observations are immutable');
END;
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS bank_no_delete
BEFORE DELETE ON bank_observations BEGIN
    SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'bank observations are immutable');
END;
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS mandate_terms_fixed
BEFORE UPDATE OF source_key, intake_hash, retained_fee_cents, score
ON mandates BEGIN
    SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'intake terms require a reviewed extension');
END;
"""

def connect(path):
    db = sqlite3.connect(str(path), timeout=30, isolation_level=None)
    db.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    db.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON")
    db.execute("PRAGMA busy_timeout = 30000")
    db.execute("PRAGMA synchronous = FULL")
    return db

def initialize(db):
    db.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL")
    db.executescript(SCHEMA)
Primary keys, unique references, and paired amounts constrain durable records
Initialize once on local storage before starting independent worker connections
Module 2: canonicalize intake and calculate deterministic screening scores
Acquire the write lock before checking source-key reuse or inserting intake
Repeated identical intake returns its original identifier without duplicating work
Module 3: advance verified workflow and atomically post commission events
Event, journal posting, and version advance commit together under one write lock
Evidence references support review while full bank matching prevents premature receipt posting
Module 4: import settled bank observations and post matched cash expenses

def import_bank(db, bank_ref, amount_cents, settled_on, source_digest):
    require_text(bank_ref)
    require_text(settled_on)
    require_text(source_digest)
    if type(amount_cents) is not int or amount_cents == 0:
        raise ValueError("bank amount must be nonzero integer cents")
    values = (bank_ref, amount_cents, settled_on, source_digest)
    with transaction(db):
        old = db.execute(
            """SELECT bank_ref, amount_cents, settled_on, source_digest
               FROM bank_observations WHERE bank_ref = ?""",
            (bank_ref,),
        ).fetchone()
        if old:
            if tuple(old) != values:
                raise ValueError("bank reference reused with different evidence")
            return bank_ref
        db.execute(
            "INSERT INTO bank_observations VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)", values
        )
        return bank_ref

def post_expense(db, command_key, amount_cents, bank_ref, evidence_ref):
    require_text(command_key)
    require_text(bank_ref)
    require_text(evidence_ref)
    if command_key.startswith("intake:"):
        raise ValueError("reserved command namespace")
    if type(amount_cents) is not int or amount_cents <= 0:
        raise ValueError("expense must be positive integer cents")
    request = {
        "operation": "expense",
        "amount_cents": amount_cents,
        "bank_ref": bank_ref,
        "evidence_ref": evidence_ref,
    }
    request_hash = digest(request)
    with transaction(db):
        if replay(db, command_key, request_hash):
            return command_key
        bank = db.execute(
            "SELECT amount_cents FROM bank_observations WHERE bank_ref = ?",
            (bank_ref,),
        ).fetchone()
        if bank is None or bank["amount_cents"] != -amount_cents:
            raise ValueError("expense requires matching settled bank debit")
        db.execute(
            """INSERT INTO events
               (command_key, request_hash, event_type, evidence_json)
               VALUES (?, ?, 'EXPENSE', ?)""",
            (command_key, request_hash, canonical(request)),
        )
        db.execute(
            """INSERT INTO journal
               (command_key, debit_account, credit_account,
                amount_cents, bank_ref)
               VALUES (?, 'EXPENSE', 'CASH', ?, ?)""",
            (command_key, amount_cents, bank_ref),
        )
        return command_key
Unique bank references and atomic rollback reject duplicate receipt or expense allocation
Importer permissions remain separate from closing review and source-document permissions
Module 5: expose balanced ledger lines and bank reconciliation totals

VIEWS = """
CREATE VIEW IF NOT EXISTS ledger_lines AS
SELECT command_key, debit_account AS account, amount_cents AS signed_cents
FROM journal
UNION ALL
SELECT command_key, credit_account AS account, -amount_cents AS signed_cents
FROM journal;

CREATE VIEW IF NOT EXISTS reconciliation AS
SELECT
    COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN account = 'CASH'
        THEN signed_cents ELSE 0 END), 0) AS book_cash_movement_cents,
    COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN account = 'AR'
        THEN signed_cents ELSE 0 END), 0) AS receivable_cents,
    COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN account = 'REVENUE'
        THEN -signed_cents ELSE 0 END), 0) AS retained_revenue_cents,
    COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN account = 'EXPENSE'
        THEN signed_cents ELSE 0 END), 0) AS expense_cents,
    COALESCE(SUM(signed_cents), 0) AS signed_balance_cents,
    (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(amount_cents), 0)
        FROM bank_observations) AS bank_movement_cents,
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM bank_observations AS b
        LEFT JOIN journal AS j ON j.bank_ref = b.bank_ref
        WHERE j.id IS NULL) AS unmatched_bank_count
FROM ledger_lines;
"""

def install_views(db):
    db.executescript(VIEWS)

def reconcile(db):
    result = dict(db.execute("SELECT * FROM reconciliation").fetchone())
    result["earned_profit_cents"] = (
        result["retained_revenue_cents"] - result["expense_cents"]
    )
    result["cash_difference_cents"] = (
        result["bank_movement_cents"] - result["book_cash_movement_cents"]
    )
    return result
Each journal record contributes equal opposite lines without separate partial inserts
Compare scoped statement movement with book movement before adding external opening cash
Module 6: test replay safety, concurrent posting, rollback, and reconciliation
Concurrent workers replay one command while uniqueness rejects a second bank allocation
Self-test is provided for execution; no execution result is asserted here

sections.heading: 4. Walk the 90-Day Cohorts and Reconcile Earned Profit to Cash
paragraphs: Treat this as a stabilized operating-quarter illustration, not a cold-start promise. Time to first deal remains three to twelve months, so the walk begins with eight inherited late-stage opportunities, no opening commission receivable, and $100,000 operator cash. Five inherited opportunities close during the quarter at $27,500 retained commission each; two fail and one remains active. New intake forms three distinct twenty-lead cohorts, one per month. Each cohort loses eight unsuitable records during screening, places six into nurture, and qualifies six. Of those six, three execute mandates and three remain in diligence. None of these new mandates closes inside the illustrated quarter. Across sixty new leads, that produces twenty-four scrubs, eighteen nurture records, nine diligence records, and nine signed mandates. Keep screening scrubs separate from failed late-stage closings: they imply different problems and consume different amounts of specialist work. The ending active inventory is thirty-seven records, comprising thirty-six new-cohort records plus the one inherited survivor. Do not annualize nine new mandates into guaranteed completions. Future quarters require sufficient conversion, new sourcing, and replenishment to replace the inherited closing inventory rather than repeatedly spending the same opening pipeline.

The quarterly revenue bridge is five closings multiplied by $27,500, producing $137,500 earned retained commissions. Annualizing that operating pace gives exactly $550,000, the Base scorecard revenue. Total quarterly operating cost is $85,937.50: $12,000 monthly fixed overhead plus $49,937.50 quarterly variable delivery, contractor, and closing costs. The fixed component sits inside the stated $3,000 to $18,000 monthly operating-overhead range; total recognized operating costs are higher because the scorecard also absorbs variable delivery expense. Allocate the quarter as $28,645.83, $28,645.83, and $28,645.84 to avoid rounding drift. Costs associated with failed opportunities are included, not quietly removed from margin. Earned quarterly owner profit is therefore $51,562.50, or 37.5 percent, reconciling to $206,250 annually. Owner distributions do not create additional operating expense inside this illustration. For comparison, the Conservative case remains $100,000 revenue less $75,000 costs, yielding $25,000 owner profit; Scaled remains $1,000,000 revenue less $500,000 costs, yielding $500,000 owner profit. The respective staffing assumptions stay one full-time operator plus three contractors for Conservative and Base, and two full-time operators plus four contractors for Scaled.

Cash collection intentionally trails earned revenue. Month 1 closes one inherited deal but receives no commission cash. Month 2 closes two and collects $55,000: the Month 1 invoice and one Month 2 invoice. Month 3 closes two and collects $55,000: the remaining Month 2 invoice and one Month 3 invoice. The final Month 3 invoice remains a $27,500 receivable scheduled for Month 4, subject to actual collection. Quarterly receipts total $110,000, so cash increases only $24,062.50 after $85,937.50 costs, ending at $124,062.50. The difference from $51,562.50 earned profit is exactly the $27,500 receivable increase. All expenses are paid in the month recognized, with no opening payables, debt service, taxes, capital purchases, or owner withdrawals in this limited bridge. Do not multiply this working-capital build by four and describe the result as annual owner profit. If collection slips another month, preserve the receivable and reduce the cash forecast instead of manufacturing a receipt. Review aging, escrow evidence, and fee disputes weekly. At the illustrated $28,645.83 monthly cash-cost pace, $100,000 covers roughly 3.49 months without receipts, making failed closings and delayed collections immediate capacity decisions rather than cosmetic dashboard exceptions.

chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #26, High-Ticket Brokerage, ranks #10 with an 88/100 Money-to-Manpower Score across 21 mapped plays. Its information edge comes from resolving ownership, authority, encumbrances, buyer capacity, and closing dependencies before competing desks do. This chapter connects official registries, commercial enrichment, reproducible evidence, and milestone tooling without treating scraped contacts as qualified buyers. Canonical annual owner profit is $25,000 Conservative, $206,250 Base, and $500,000 Scaled; revenue means retained transaction commissions, never underlying asset consideration. Use a provenance-first waterfall, explicit licensing checks, and independent escrow verification. The mapped social-account and Section 179D plays receive separate transferability and eligibility tests, preventing a seductive lead list from becoming an uncloseable mandate.

sections.heading: 1. Resolve the seller, asset, and authority before buying another lead
paragraphs: Start every exclusive mandate with an identity spine, not a contact spreadsheet. Assign a deal identifier, record the seller's exact legal name and formation jurisdiction, then attach the state entity number, asset identifier, signing authority, and expected closing venue. Separate registered agent, officer, beneficial owner, and authorized seller; a registry hit establishes neither ownership of the offered asset nor permission to sell it. Obtain the engagement letter, organizational documents, and seller authorization directly, then compare them with official records. For equipment, preserve serial numbers and invoice chains; for aircraft, use the registration and airframe identifiers; for property, use parcel and recorded instrument references. For business sales, distinguish an asset purchase from a securities transaction before selecting the broker's operating structure. Exchange Act registration and the conditional M&A broker exemption in 15 U.S.C. 78o(b)(13) require a transaction-specific assessment; the exemption does not erase state requirements or permit custody of client funds. Place every conflict into an exception queue with a named resolver. The first deliverable is a defensible identity packet that an escrow officer, buyer, and transaction adviser can independently follow without relying on the salesperson's memory.

Treat each registry as an instrument with a narrow measurement range. A Secretary of State record supports entity existence and filing status, while a UCC search supports a particular debtor-name and jurisdiction inquiry. Neither substitutes for a lien release, title opinion, or ownership representation. Apply the adopted state versions of UCC Sections 9-301, 9-307, 9-503, and 9-506 when deciding where and under which name to search; include former names and merger history when the facts require them. County recorder indexes can lag document submission, and asset registries can lag a recent transfer. Request certified searches or specialist title work when closing exposure justifies the expense. PACER supplies federal court records, not a complete national judgment or litigation search; add the relevant state courts and bankruptcy review. OFAC screening likewise requires identity resolution, not a binary decision from a similar surname. Record search parameters, retrieval time, source update date when exposed, and coverage limits. Recheck material facts before accepting a mandate and again before releasing closing instructions. If the record conflicts with the seller's story, stop distributing that assertion rather than silently overwriting the evidence with a more convenient commercial database entry.

Use the directory below as a research routing map, not a promise that every source has a supported API or immediate publication. Its refresh entries distinguish source publication from the desk's polling policy. Assign one owner to maintain endpoint documentation, permitted use, account requirements, and current prices quarterly. Public access does not imply permission for unlimited extraction, commercial redistribution, or unrestricted personal-data use. Where only a browser portal exists, use authorized manual retrieval or an approved records provider rather than defeating access controls. Download a reusable official bulk file once when offered, retain its publication date, and update only the changed records. Conditional requests and shared caching reduce load and prevent several contractors from paying for the same document. For an illustrative 40-mandate research queue, a $15 initial records allowance per mandate creates a $600 procurement envelope, not a claim about registry pricing. Escalate certified searches against specific closing exposure instead of purchasing them indiscriminately. When a source is unavailable, label the fact as awaiting evidence, identify the alternate official source, and assign a deadline. A stale record may support historical analysis; it must not masquerade as current clearance for a high-value transfer.

sections.heading: 2. Buy enrichment only after the mandate survives primary-source checks
paragraphs: Build the enrichment waterfall around an identified company and a documented purpose. Begin with the entity spine and company website, then add commercial company identifiers, relevant executives, and permitted business contact channels. OpenCorporates can improve cross-jurisdiction discovery, D&B Direct+ can supply licensed business identifiers and attributes, and Crunchbase can suggest ownership or funding events. None should silently replace a primary document. For each attribute, store the provider, retrieval date, matching inputs, confidence, and redistribution permission. A matching name is weaker than agreement across jurisdiction, address, domain, and registration number. Distinguish a buyer's announced fund size from available acquisition capital, and distinguish a portfolio company's employee count from the parent organization's purchasing authority. Contact enrichment follows qualification rather than preceding it. People Data Labs and Hunter can support permitted discovery and verification under their current terms, but a deliverable address does not establish permission, relevance, or buyer interest. Route ambiguous records to a human researcher instead of spraying outreach across possible identities. Maintain suppression records and apply channel-specific rules, including CAN-SPAM for commercial email and applicable restrictions on automated calls or texts. The desired output is a small, explainable buyer shortlist, not a maximal collection of personal records.

Price the waterfall by accepted evidence, not nominal API credits. Consider an illustrative batch of 200 company candidates: official checks eliminate 80, commercial company matching resolves 90 of the remaining 120, and human review accepts 60 for outreach research. At assumed internal budgeting rates of $0.20 for each of 120 company lookups and $0.10 for each of 60 contact verifications, variable API spend is $30. These are planning assumptions, not vendor quotations, and exclude subscriptions, minimum commitments, registry fees, and researcher time. If 12 recipients become qualified buyer conversations, that narrow variable cost is $2.50 per conversation; the fully loaded acquisition cost remains higher. Log every lookup against a deal or research campaign so an unused annual subscription cannot disappear inside overhead. Purchase a second provider only when its incremental matches justify the incremental expense and permitted usage. When two sources disagree, preserve both claims and seek stronger evidence rather than averaging identities. Cache only for the contractually allowed period, respect deletion obligations, and remove unnecessary personal attributes. The cheapest reliable fallback is often a targeted call through the company's published switchboard, not a third bulk-data contract.

The mapped play aged_high_karma_social_account_brokerage needs an explicit asset-rights test before anyone prices audience access. Account age, karma, followers, and verification badges are observations, not transferable property rights or proof of authentic influence. Reddit, LinkedIn, X, and TikTok impose different account, identity, advertising, and transfer restrictions; inspect the current rules for the exact proposed transaction. This desk excludes fabricated personas, manufactured reputation, proxy-based filter evasion, and covert coordinated promotion. It does not operationalize account fleets or promise search placement or model citations. Instead, evaluate permitted creator-business acquisitions, licensed content, disclosed sponsorships, or platform-supported transfers with written authority. An illustrative $80,000 permitted business acquisition at a 10% retained commission produces $8,000 broker revenue, not $80,000. If expected diligence costs are $2,000, the remaining $6,000 is transaction contribution before shared overhead and other costs, not the chapter's annual owner profit. Require seller-authorized analytics, audience-quality sampling, content-rights schedules, and an escrow condition covering the supported transfer method. If platform permission or identity continuity cannot be established, exclude the account from the sale and value independently transferable assets instead. If those assets cannot support the economics, decline the mandate rather than substituting a concealment technique.

callout.body: Spend research money where a stronger record changes mandate acceptance, buyer matching, or closing probability.

sections.heading: 3. Build an auditable evidence pipeline instead of a fragile scraping stack
paragraphs: A small desk can operate a durable pipeline with Python's urllib.request, json, csv, sqlite3, hashlib, and logging modules, plus an authorized CRM or spreadsheet for workflow visibility. Keep raw evidence separate from normalized assertions. A source record should contain a source identifier, request parameters with secrets removed, retrieval timestamp in UTC, response status, publication date when available, content hash, and permitted retention period. An assertion should link an entity or asset to a field, value, effective date, evidence reference, and reviewer. A SHA-256 hash helps detect later file changes; it does not prove that the original statement was true. Use stable keys and unique constraints to prevent repeated imports from creating duplicate buyers or duplicated milestone tasks. Do not place API keys, full bank details, or unnecessary identity documents in logs. Protect stored evidence with account-level access controls and encrypted storage, and keep client-specific workspaces separate. Test backup restoration, not merely backup creation. For an illustrative 300 evidence packets averaging 2 MB, raw storage is about 600 MB before versions and backups; document quality, permission management, and reviewer time dominate the economics, not disk capacity.

Design connectors to fail visibly and narrowly. Set connection and read timeouts, bound response sizes, validate content types, and reject schema changes that would silently move an address into an ownership field. Use per-provider concurrency limits and exponential backoff with jitter; honor Retry-After and never rotate identities to defeat quotas. Quarantine authentication failures until the account owner resolves them. A daily scheduled run is a desk policy, not evidence that the underlying registry updates daily. Preserve the last successful retrieval and display its age beside every material assertion. Build contract tests from permitted fixtures covering empty results, multiple matches, revoked credentials, expired pagination tokens, and truncated downloads. Use sqlite3 transactions so a failed import does not leave half a buyer cohort marked as verified. Track fetched records, accepted matches, exceptions, cost units, and human review minutes as separate counters. If a provider disappears, route affected cases to the documented manual procedure rather than allowing automated buyer matching to continue on stale attributes. Reconciliation should expose disagreements between sources, not smooth them away into a deceptively confident score. A useful automation result is an accurate exception list with owners and deadlines, even when no record qualifies for unattended acceptance.

Connect evidence to a closing state machine: mandate signed, identity resolved, buyer qualified, diligence opened, definitive documents executed, funding confirmed, escrow conditions satisfied, and commission settled. Each transition needs a responsible person and a supporting artifact. Buyer-seller matching ranks fit against documented criteria; it does not invent capacity. Document checklists must distinguish received, reviewed, accepted, expired, and superseded materials. For an NCNDA, record the covered parties, introduced opportunity, effective period, exceptions, and acknowledged delivery; a generic template cannot establish every commission claim. Keep underlying purchase money outside the desk's ordinary operating account, using properly authorized escrow and asset-specific handling arrangements. Verify escrow instructions through independently obtained contact details and a second communication channel; an email thread alone cannot authenticate changed bank details. Diagnostic tools test systems, not counterparties' honesty: a valid TLS certificate proves neither escrow authority nor account ownership. Before closing, rerun the material entity, sanctions, lien, and authority checks under the transaction team's required timetable. After settlement, reconcile the escrow statement, commission entitlement, co-broker allocations, and bank receipt. Preserve the evidence needed to explain the retained amount while deleting personal information that no longer has a justified retention purpose.

sections.heading: 4. Screen allocation opportunities and reconcile tooling to retained commissions
paragraphs: The mapped play section_179d_municipal_deduction_allocation_arbitrage concerns documented allocations to eligible designers, not a marketplace for freely transferable deductions. Under 26 U.S.C. 179D, first identify the qualifying building owner, eligible property, designer contribution, and applicable construction and placed-in-service dates. The statute terminates eligibility for property whose construction begins after June 30, 2026; document the applicable construction-start analysis rather than assuming every public retrofit remains eligible. Government ownership and specified tax-exempt ownership require their own eligibility analysis. IRS organization records, public procurement awards, building permits, and owner-authorized Portfolio Manager data help identify candidates, but none establishes a deduction amount. Obtain the design contract, scope of services, allocation authorization, qualifying technical calculations, and certification required under applicable rules. Determine whether prevailing-wage and apprenticeship requirements affect the available amount, and retain the substantiation supporting that determination. Municipal staff may possess useful records without possessing authority to sign the allocation. Confirm the owner's delegation and procurement requirements before proposing compensation. Where a federal contract is implicated, examine the actual solicitation and contract clauses, including applicable contingent-fee restrictions, rather than treating public-sector access as permission to charge a success fee. Every eligibility conclusion belongs to a documented project review.

Use unit math to prevent deduction amounts from leaking into brokerage revenue. An illustrative 100,000-square-foot building multiplied by an independently substantiated hypothetical $2.00-per-square-foot applicable amount produces a $200,000 deduction before other applicable limitations. That assumed rate is not a published rate for a particular tax year, and the deduction is neither a $200,000 cash payment nor operator revenue. Actual tax benefit depends on the recipient's tax position and applicable limitations. A separately contracted $6,000 fixed documentation fee would compensate defined services, subject to eligibility, procurement, and professional-scope requirements. It is outside this volume's retained-transaction-commission scorecard and must not be inserted into the canonical cases. If a proposed contingent arrangement is impermissible or the allocation is doubtful, pause the allocation, obtain independent tax review, and offer fixed-fee documentation support only for eligible projects. Do not cure an ineligible project by renaming the fee. Record who prepares the calculation, who independently certifies the technical work, who authorizes allocation, and who claims the deduction. If those responsibilities collapse into one unsupported broker assertion, the opportunity has failed diligence regardless of the potential headline deduction or enthusiasm of the lead source.

Keep the canonical operating model fixed while using local assumptions to test throughput. Conservative retained commissions are $100,000, with $75,000 total costs and $25,000 owner profit at 25%, supported by 1 FT + 3 C. Base retained commissions are $550,000, with $343,750 total costs and $206,250 owner profit at 37.5%, also with 1 FT + 3 C. Scaled retained commissions are $1,000,000, with $500,000 total costs and $500,000 owner profit at 50%, supported by 2 FT + 4 C. chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #26, High-Ticket Brokerage, ranks #10 with an 88/100 Money-to-Manpower Score across a portfolio of 21 mapped plays. Its leverage comes from specialist mandates and retained transaction commissions, never from counting client asset values as revenue. Annual owner profit is $25,000 Conservative, $206,250 Base, and $500,000 Scaled. This chapter converts licensing boundaries, agency disclosures, anti-circumvention evidence, and escrow instructions into executable deal controls. It also separates legitimate ticket allocation resale from purchase-limit evasion and distinguishes authorized WOTC screening from unsupported credit claims. Use the contract matrices and verbatim scripts before soliciting counterparties: a signed mandate cannot cure an unlicensed activity, an unavailable exemption, or a commission trigger that never occurred.

sections.heading: 1. Classify the Asset, Activity, Jurisdiction, and Exemption Before Soliciting
paragraphs: Open every mandate with an activity map, not a generic broker agreement. Record the asset, ownership structure, seller location, buyer locations, solicitation channels, compensation formula, and every task the operator will perform. Negotiating an equipment sale, marketing membership interests, placing acquisition debt, and selling a business with real estate are different activities even when they share one closing date. A percentage success fee attached to a securities transaction is a strong registration warning; calling it consulting does not change the underlying conduct. Assign each workstream to a named licensed professional or a documented exemption analysis before circulating identifying materials. Store the result in a deal register with jurisdiction, authority, expiration date, permitted acts, prohibited acts, and reviewer. FINRA BrokerCheck, SEC Investment Adviser Public Disclosure, and state regulator searches answer different questions; an adviser listing does not establish broker-dealer authority. Verify the actual contracting entity and responsible individual, not merely a familiar trade name. The practical deliverable is a one-page permission map that tells the researcher, originator, negotiator, and closing coordinator exactly what each may do. Pause only the affected workstream when an unresolved boundary appears; preserve authorized documentation work without continuing restricted solicitation.

For securities-based business sales, start with Exchange Act Section 15(a), 15 U.S.C. 78o(a), then test the federal M&A broker exemption in Section 15(b)(13) rather than assuming all private-company sales qualify. The eligible privately held company definition includes reporting-status conditions and a preceding-fiscal-year size test: EBITDA below $25 million or gross revenue below $250 million, subject to statutory inflation adjustments when applicable. Preserve the underlying statements and calculation. The broker must reasonably believe the buyer will control and actively manage the business; a passive minority investment does not become eligible through contract wording. Examine the statutory control presumptions without treating a percentage alone as proof of active management. Excluded activities include custody of transaction funds or securities, public offerings, specified shell-company transactions, and binding a party to the transaction. Providing acquisition financing is excluded; assisting with third-party financing has separate conditions and compensation disclosures. Dual representation requires clear written disclosure and written consent from both parties. Buyer-group formation and disciplinary history require their own checks. Document each condition individually, including required information access for securities exchanges. Federal relief does not automatically satisfy state securities registration requirements or authorize unrelated capital raising.

Build the state analysis around conduct and transaction nexus, not the broker's mailing address. California Business and Professions Code Section 10131 includes specified compensated activities involving real property and business opportunities; an asset sale can therefore create a real estate licensing question even without a stock transfer. Other states draw different business-broker and securities boundaries. Obtain a state-specific answer for solicitation, negotiation, local property, referral compensation, and remote personnel. Aircraft, vessels, motor vehicles, alcohol-related businesses, and regulated professional practices add sector-specific ownership, dealer, or transfer requirements. Do not infer authority from a prior deal in another state. Identify whether the operator represents the seller, buyer, or both, then deliver required agency disclosures before the relevant conduct. Keep purchase deposits out of the operating account. Use an appropriately authorized escrow provider under written instructions, after determining which trust-account and client-fund rules govern the transaction. Outsourcing escrow does not erase licensing duties or permit an exempt M&A broker to take custody. Allocate a specific budget for this classification work from the $15,000–$100,000 startup range; discovering a licensing defect after a signed purchase agreement can destroy the entire commission.

sections.heading: 2. Draft a Collectible Mandate and an Evidence-Based NCNDA
paragraphs: The exclusive mandate should define the represented party, scheduled assets or interests, territory, authorized marketing channels, excluded counterparties, engagement period, termination rights, and the operator's limited authority. State expressly that the broker cannot bind either party or alter definitive transaction documents. Describe exclusivity precisely: an exclusive agency and an exclusive right to sell can produce different commission outcomes. Attach a dated list of preexisting buyer relationships and decide how those relationships affect fees. Define the fee base using consideration actually covered by the mandate, including the treatment of assumed debt, rollover equity, earnouts, working-capital adjustments, and seller notes. A clean illustrative clause reads: 'The closing commission equals five percent of cash purchase consideration actually received by Seller at closing, excluding taxes, reimbursed expenses, and working-capital adjustments; contingent consideration produces a commission only when Seller receives it.' On $1 million of covered cash consideration, that formula produces $50,000 before any agreed co-broker split, not $1 million of operator revenue. Specify whether the stated commission is gross or retained, who pays it, when the invoice issues, and which settlement instruction authorizes its disbursement. Address failed closings explicitly instead of assuming effort alone earns the success fee.

Treat the nondisclosure and non-circumvention agreement, or NCNDA, as a scoped evidence instrument rather than a threat pasted across every email. Identify protected information, permitted evaluation purposes, authorized recipients, reasonable security duties, and exclusions for information already known, independently developed, or lawfully obtained. Require advisers to receive information under appropriate confidentiality duties, with responsibility allocated for onward disclosure. Non-circumvention should protect specifically introduced counterparties and the defined transaction opportunity for a reasonable period, subject to applicable state law. It should not claim ownership of an entire industry or block unrelated future commerce. A usable starting clause reads: 'For twelve months after termination, the agreed commission remains payable on a covered transaction completed with a counterparty first introduced in writing during the engagement and identified in the termination schedule, except scheduled preexisting relationships.' Whether that tail is enforceable depends on governing law, licensing, causation standards, and the complete agreement. Preserve introduction emails, accepted buyer lists, meeting records, and data-room access receipts. DocuSign authenticates execution workflows; it does not prove that an introduction caused a sale. Review disputed contacts promptly and maintain a jointly acknowledged exception register rather than manufacturing exclusivity after negotiations succeed.

Allocate representations to the party that can verify them. The seller warrants authority to sell and the accuracy of identified materials subject to negotiated qualifications; the broker undertakes specified diligence and accurate transmission without inventing operating results. Require source labels and dated corrections for teasers, forecasts, and buyer questions. A liability cap should state its calculation, covered claims, aggregation period, and negotiated exceptions; mandatory law may prevent limitations for fraud or other conduct. Align indemnities, defense control, settlement consent, and insurance rather than layering contradictory promises. Select governing law, forum, service methods, escalation timing, and any arbitration rules with enforceability and collection costs in mind. Address temporary relief without promising that a court will grant it. Separate seller-owned documents, broker-owned templates, commissioned analyses, licensed databases, and buyer personal information. Give each participant only the rights needed for the transaction, with retention schedules and litigation-hold exceptions. A Google Drive folder with public links is not a controlled data room. Use role-based access in SharePoint or a dedicated deal room, revoke departed users, and preserve access logs. The contract should explain what survives termination: payment obligations, confidentiality, document retention, dispute provisions, and the narrowly drafted tail.

callout.title: Protect the Commission Before the Buyer Becomes Valuable
callout.body: Experienced intermediaries create evidence while relationships are cooperative, not after parties discover they can close without another introduction.
items: Send the protected-counterparty schedule with the first authorized introduction, and obtain acknowledgment before granting access to sensitive seller documents.

sections.heading: 3. Use Verbatim Outreach Scripts and Reject Allocation-Limit Evasion
paragraphs: For commercial email, apply CAN-SPAM, 15 U.S.C. 7704, to business recipients as well as consumers. Use accurate routing information, a nondeceptive subject, required advertising identification where applicable, a valid physical postal address, and a working opt-out. Honor opt-outs within ten business days and retain a suppression record across vendors. Use this initial message after substituting verified facts: 'Subject: Acquisition interest in your precision-machining business. This is a commercial solicitation from Northline Transaction Services. I represent a buyer seeking an operating machining company in Ohio; I do not represent you. Would you consider a confidential conversation about ownership objectives? I can first provide our identity, authority, and process. No documents or payment are needed to answer. Reply stop to end our marketing emails. Our mailing address appears below.' Append the actual postal address, not a fictional suite. Do not claim an identified buyer unless the mandate supports that claim. For calls and texts, assess the TCPA, 47 U.S.C. 227, FCC rules, applicable FTC requirements, and state restrictions before selecting technology. Purchased contact data is not evidence of consent for a channel requiring it. A manual call does not automatically escape do-not-call or state solicitation requirements.

Open a permitted discovery call with role clarity: 'I represent the seller for this transaction. Before discussing identity or pricing, may I confirm your entity, acquisition role, preferred communication channel, and whether you are evaluating for your own account or another party?' Follow with: 'What operating experience, decision authority, funding sources, and closing timetable can you document? We can accept redacted evidence through the secure room; please do not email account credentials or complete bank statements.' For seller discovery, use: 'Who has authority to engage an intermediary, what interests or assets may be sold, which advisers are already retained, and which counterparties must be excluded from our introduction schedule?' Then state: 'Our proposed compensation and representation will be disclosed in writing before covered work begins. We cannot promise a closing or a valuation.' Ask separately about call recording and apply the relevant state consent rules before recording. Log source, time, role, communication preferences, and any suppression request in HubSpot or Salesforce. For a declined approach, finish with: 'Understood. I will stop marketing contact through this channel and record your preference.' Do not turn discovery into pressure for deposits, privileged documents, or disclosure of another bidder's confidential terms.

The mapped play verified_fan_ticketing_and_drop_allocation_farming requires a hard boundary between lawful resale and evading access controls. The proposed hundred-account amplification using residential proxies, aged profiles, or virtual cards to defeat ticket limits is not an operating method to implement. The BOTS Act, 15 U.S.C. 45c, prohibits specified circumvention of online ticket controls and certain downstream sales involving unlawfully obtained tickets. Ticketmaster Verified Fan, AXS, U.S. Mint, and luxury releases also have distinct eligibility, transfer, and purchase rules; the ticket statute does not automatically govern collectible coins. Use genuine independent purchasers only when program terms permit their participation and any resale. Distinct addresses or card issuer identifiers do not cure coordinated limit evasion. Ten independent eligible purchasers each buying two permitted tickets at $200 create $4,000 of acquisition cost, not operator revenue. A lawful $6,000 resale produces $2,000 gross spread before fees and losses; an authorized brokerage retaining ten percent instead recognizes $600 commission, not that spread. Verify inventory ownership and transfer rights before making wholesale commitments. If aggregation, resale, or transfer is prohibited, abandon the allocation strategy and broker already transferable inventory through authorized channels. Never market a presale commitment as certain delivery when allocation remains unresolved.

sections.heading: 4. Separate Tax-Service Boundaries, Secure Escrow, and Reconcile Retained Fees
paragraphs: The mapped play wotc_hourly_payroll_tax_credit_contingency_engine must separate employer-authorized WOTC screening from Section 41 research-credit substantiation and from transaction brokerage. Under 26 U.S.C. 51, verify program authorization for the employee's actual start date before quoting eligibility; Section 51(c)(4) states a termination date for individuals beginning work after December 31, 2025, so later starts require an enacted extension before relying on renewed eligibility. Do not assume a software vendor's marketing establishes current authority. For an authorized period, Form 8850 prescreening generally must be completed on or before the offer date, with the certification request submitted to the state workforce agency within twenty-eight days after work begins, subject to applicable relief. An ordinary qualifying worker with $6,000 of qualified first-year wages and at least 400 hours can generate a $2,400 credit; ten such workers produce $24,000 before employer limitations. A hypothetical permitted fifteen-percent service fee would be $3,600, not $24,000 revenue. Review Circular 230 Section 10.27 and applicable professional fee restrictions before using contingency pricing. Separately document Section 41 activities, qualified expenses, funding, exclusions, and Section 280C coordination. Fall back to fixed-fee documentation under independent tax review, exclude unsupported claims, and keep these service fees outside the brokerage scorecard.

Closing control begins before anyone receives wiring instructions. Identify the escrow provider's legal entity, authority, account title, permitted services, and dispute process using independent sources. A familiar email signature is insufficient. Obtain instructions through the agreed secure channel, verify them through a previously authenticated telephone number, and require two-person review for changes. Never verify a changed account using the telephone number supplied in the change request. For equipment collateral, use the applicable state's enacted UCC Article 9 to determine debtor location, search scope, perfection issues, and release requirements; registry searches for titled assets may require additional work. A financing statement search alone does not establish clean ownership. Match payoff letters, lien releases, title evidence, purchase documents, and disbursement conditions before funding. Escrow should release the broker's fee only under consistent executed instructions and the agreed trigger. If a seller alleges circumvention, preserve the disputed amount only where the escrow agreement and applicable law authorize that treatment; the broker cannot unilaterally freeze client money. After closing, reconcile the settlement statement, escrow confirmation, invoice, and bank receipt. Record chargebacks, clawbacks, co-broker payments, and deferred consideration separately so collected cash does not conceal an unresolved obligation.

Use retained commissions to reconcile the canonical scenarios, with transaction counts treated as illustrative operating assumptions. Conservative requires five closings retaining $20,000 each: $100,000 revenue less $75,000 total operating costs equals $25,000 annual owner net profit at 25% margin with 1 FT + 3 C. Base requires eleven closings retaining $50,000 each: $550,000 revenue less $343,750 costs equals $206,250 profit at 37.5% with the same staffing. Scaled requires twenty closings retaining $50,000 each: $1,000,000 revenue less $500,000 costs equals $500,000 profit at 50% with 2 FT + 4 C, six people total. Asset values never enter those revenue totals. Contractor headcounts describe capacity, not four full salaries or guaranteed availability. The $3,000–$18,000 monthly opex range is a planning input, not a substitute for the complete annual cost reconciliation, which must include variable delivery and acquisition costs without double counting. With first deal timing of three to twelve months, retain cash for failed mandates and delayed closings. Automate buyer-seller matching, milestone reminders, and document checklists, but require accountable review of licensing and wire changes. Track mandates signed, qualified buyers, diligence exits, collected commissions, and dispute exposure weekly; a large pipeline cannot pay bills until the contractual fee is earned and collected.

chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #26, High-Ticket Brokerage, ranks #10 with an 88/100 Money-to-Manpower Score across 21 mapped plays. Its automation advantage is disciplined coordination, not autonomous negotiation: Python workers collect evidence, rank buyer fit, maintain document checklists, and surface stalled milestones while people control representations and settlement. This chapter develops two tax-credit placement plays without treating credit face value, buyer wires, or asset consideration as brokerage revenue. sections.heading: 1. Build an evidence ledger before automating buyer introductions
paragraphs: Start with one exclusive mandate, one asset category, and a written commission schedule. Candidate #26 covers 21 mapped plays, but a four-person team should not launch 21 intake systems simultaneously. The full-time principal owns mandates, consequential representations, negotiations, and release decisions; three contractors cover research, document operations, and buyer development. Contractors are fractional capacity, not three additional full-time salaries. Use HubSpot or Pipedrive for relationship state and a separate evidence ledger for source documents, permissions, provenance, and review decisions. Give every mandate, legal entity, asset, document version, and introduction an immutable identifier. A signed NCNDA can support confidentiality and anti-circumvention obligations, but it cannot establish a brokerage license, repair defective agency disclosure, or replace an enforceable fee agreement. Before ingestion, the principal records the asset-specific licensing analysis and permitted activities. Securities-related M&A requires attention to Exchange Act Section 15(a), any applicable Section 15(b)(13) exemption conditions, and state rules. Real estate and other regulated assets need separate treatment. Automate routing only after these classifications exist, because the same introductory email can represent a different regulated activity when the underlying asset changes. Reject incomplete mandate records rather than letting the model invent missing authority.

Implement the intake path as signed webhook, durable event record, Python worker, validation result, review task, and CRM update. Python's hmac and hashlib can verify a provider's documented signature scheme; time validates timestamp tolerance, while json parses an explicitly limited request body. Persist a unique provider event identifier before acknowledging receipt. A small single-worker installation can use sqlite3 transactions and a unique constraint for deduplication; distributed workers need a datastore supporting their concurrency requirements. Do not claim exactly-once delivery: instead, make state transitions idempotent and reconcile uncertain external writes. urllib.request can call public APIs with timeouts, and decimal.Decimal should handle commission arithmetic. Save source URLs, retrieval timestamps, content hashes, and access permissions alongside extracted facts. An LLM receives redacted documents as evidence, never instructions from embedded text. Its structured response contains extracted fields, supporting page references, and explicit missing-field flags. Ordinary Python validators enforce types, allowed statuses, date order, and amount bounds before any CRM write. Missing evidence creates a review task rather than a fabricated answer. Keep secrets outside records and prompts, and scope each service account to the minimum objects its worker must touch.

Buyer matching should begin with deterministic eligibility filters, followed by a transparent ranking model. Filter jurisdiction, asset type, check size, closing window, mandate restrictions, and verified acquisition authority before scoring strategic fit. An illustrative score assigns 35 points to documented investment criteria, 25 to available capital evidence, 20 to timing, and 20 to relevant execution history. These weights are operating assumptions, not predictions of closing probability. The LLM summarizes why a candidate fits and cites the buyer profile fields; it does not certify funds or infer tax capacity from wealth signals. Require a human to approve the first external introduction and every material change to deal claims. Preserve the approved teaser hash so later outreach cannot silently acquire stronger assertions. A referral loop starts only after a successful introduction or completed milestone, with permission to request another relevant buyer or seller. Measure qualified responses and completed diligence, not scraped addresses. Track rejected matches by reason and update filters weekly, keeping the original rejection evidence. If ranking quality deteriorates, disable the ranking layer and return to a saved, manually reviewed shortlist while retaining the same mandate and introduction records.

sections.heading: 2. Automate credit origination without inventing transferability or inventory profits
paragraphs: For transferable_tax_credit_brokerage_syndication, assemble an origination watchlist from federal DOE and EPA project resources, actual ISO or utility interconnection queues, state film offices, and historic-preservation registries. DOE and EPA are discovery sources, not a universal interconnection queue or proof that a project generated transferable credits. Use published downloads and permitted APIs before scraping; cache responses, respect access terms, and stop collection when permission or source integrity is doubtful. Resolve project companies through documented ownership relationships rather than fuzzy names alone. A queue position, film announcement, or historic designation creates a lead, not a saleable credit. The worker should extract project status, location, owner, program, evidence date, and the next verification question. A researcher then confirms whether the relevant taxpayer generated an eligible credit, whether certification or registration is complete, and whether a buyer can use it. Federal Section 6418 and state transfer programs belong in separate rule sets. Record the governing tax year and program version because eligibility, caps, deadlines, and administrative practices change. Until these checks pass, the system labels the opportunity as origination research and suppresses executable buyer offers.

The advertised sourcing band of $0.82 to $0.88 and placement band of $0.92 to $0.96 per credit dollar requires careful transaction design. On $1,000,000 face value, those bands imply $820,000 to $880,000 of seller-side pricing and $920,000 to $960,000 of buyer-side pricing, with a theoretical $40,000 to $140,000 gross difference before expenses. That difference is neither automatically earned nor automatically brokerage revenue. Under Section 6418, an eligible taxpayer transfers credits directly to an unrelated buyer for cash; a transferee cannot subsequently transfer the purchased credit. Therefore, do not implement a federal buy-and-resell chain. Structure a direct transfer with simultaneous escrow disbursements and an expressly disclosed commission that the parties accept. A $30,000 retained commission is $30,000 revenue, regardless of credit face value or wires passing through independent escrow. Require buyer funding before release and never warehouse unhedged credits on the operator's balance sheet. Where the mandate requires non-cancelable tax-credit insurance, inspect the bound policy, exclusions, limits, insured parties, and cancellation provisions before scheduling settlement. If suitable coverage or direct-transfer mechanics are unavailable, suspend the transaction; insurance does not itself validate eligibility.

For state_film_historic_brownfield_tax_credit_brokerage, build a jurisdiction-specific placement checklist instead of copying the federal workflow. Georgia film credits, Louisiana motion-picture credits, state historic rehabilitation credits, and brownfield incentives can have different certification, assignment, taxpayer, carryforward, notification, and transfer-frequency requirements. Federal historic rehabilitation credits do not become outright transferable merely because a state program permits assignments. The matching worker asks for the certified amount, credit year, usable tax type, permitted transferee, remaining life, prior assignments, and required agency acknowledgments. A designated tax specialist verifies those answers against current primary authority and the actual certificate before the principal authorizes a term sheet. Illustratively, placing $500,000 face value at $0.90 produces $450,000 of buyer consideration; a separately contracted 3% fee on face value yields $15,000 operator revenue, not $450,000. Escrow instructions must identify who pays that fee and avoid counting it twice. If certification, buyer usability, or assignment restrictions fail diligence, suspend settlement under the agreed contingencies and rematch only verified eligible credits. Do not guarantee tax savings. Keep this state placement funnel distinct from federal transfers so one successful closing cannot incorrectly train the matching rules for another jurisdiction.

sections.heading: 3. Connect document checklists, closing milestones, and permissioned growth loops
paragraphs: Build fulfillment around a finite-state machine rather than a collection of calendar reminders. Useful states include mandate signed, buyer screened, teaser approved, diligence opened, conditions outstanding, settlement ready, closed, and suspended. Each transition requires specified evidence, a responsible person, and a permitted actor. The document worker compares an asset-specific checklist with actual file versions, flags missing signatures and stale certificates, and drafts a precise deficiency request. It cannot decide that a missing condition is commercially immaterial. DocuSign completion events can populate signature evidence, but a completed envelope does not prove every closing condition has been satisfied. Track deadline origin, timezone, responsible counterparty, escalation date, and supporting clause. When a deadline changes, retain both versions and the authorizing communication. Escrow providers remain responsible for their contracted custody and release functions; the brokerage tracks status without treating a webhook as authority to move money. Verify changed bank instructions through an established contact using an independently sourced number. A suspicious change freezes settlement communications until resolved. During an outage, the operations contractor exports the last approved checklist and runs a manual exception log that is reconciled before automated transitions resume.

Distribution should reuse verified knowledge without publishing confidential inventory. Build programmatic pages around specific acquisition criteria, jurisdictions, process timelines, and evidence requirements, with human-reviewed source links and an update date. Do not auto-publish seller identities, buyer tax positions, unsupported returns, or confidential transaction examples. A practical loop starts with a useful buyer checklist, captures permission for a narrowly defined update, asks for acquisition criteria, and returns a reviewed relevant opportunity. After a successful milestone, request a permissioned introduction to one comparable counterparty. This is a referral mechanism, not an assumption of viral growth. For outbound email, apply CAN-SPAM requirements including accurate headers, truthful subject lines, required sender information, and working opt-out processing. Maintain one suppression ledger across contractors and delivery vendors; honor opt-outs within the statutory deadline and preferably immediately. Automated calls and texts require their own channel-specific review rather than borrowing email rules. Illustratively, 200 eligible emails producing 20 replies, eight qualified conversations, and two diligence starts demonstrate routing yield, not two future closings. Inspect rejection reasons and complaints before increasing volume, and stop a sequence when a recipient's eligibility or permission changes.

Treat every integration failure as a recoverable business event. Retry transient network errors with bounded exponential backoff and jitter, honor provider rate-limit instructions, and move persistent failures to an exception queue with an owner and deadline. Never retry wire instructions or client-facing messages blindly after a timeout: first determine whether the original action succeeded. Store the intended operation, external object identifier, request hash, attempt count, and reconciliation result. A malformed model response should trigger deterministic extraction or manual review, not an increasingly permissive prompt. Repeated model disagreement on credit amounts, parties, or restrictions disables that workflow until the underlying cause is understood. Keep a small evaluation set of previously reviewed documents, including amended certificates, duplicate projects, conflicting signatures, and adversarial embedded instructions. Re-run it before changing prompts, parsers, or model versions. Measure field accuracy separately from narrative fluency and sample low-confidence and high-value cases more heavily. Log who corrected each field and why. The principal receives a daily exception digest showing blocked closings, aged diligence, changed instructions, and overdue reviews, while contractors receive only the tasks and documents needed for their assigned responsibilities.

sections.heading: 4. Prove the 70% threshold and scale retained commissions, not transaction volume
paragraphs: Measure automation against a fixed, observed basket of repetitive work. The illustrative weekly baseline below contains 1,000 manual minutes across research, qualification, document checking, milestone tracking, distribution preparation, and reconciliation. Automation displaces 850 minutes but adds 110 minutes of review, leaving 150 minutes of untouched manual work plus 110 review minutes. Net reduction is therefore (1,000 minus 260) divided by 1,000, or 74%. This is a testable workload target, not a claim that software conducts 74% of negotiation or professional judgment. Include correction time, failed runs, duplicate cleanup, and contractor supervision in the measured remainder. Establish the baseline with a representative sample before deployment and use the same task definitions afterward. If the weekly basket changes materially, publish separate old-basket and new-basket results rather than declaring an artificial improvement. Sample all consequential outputs for human authorization and use risk-weighted checks on routine extraction. A rising correction rate consumes the apparent savings immediately. Pause the weakest workflow when net reduction falls below the target, retain the working automations, and restore the manual procedure until the defective rule or source is repaired.

Price each automated run explicitly before choosing a model or orchestration vendor. Assume, solely for budgeting, 4,000 input tokens at $2 per million and 1,000 output tokens at $8 per million: model cost is $0.008 plus $0.008, or $0.016. Add $0.004 for allocated execution and storage to obtain $0.020 per successful machine attempt. These are illustrative rates, not a quoted vendor tariff. With a 10% expected additional-attempt allowance, machine cost averages $0.022 per completed run. Two minutes of reviewer time at $60 per hour adds $2.00, producing $2.022 per reviewed run, or $202.20 for 100 runs. That review-heavy example is separate from the weekly workload basket and should not be substituted into it without matching task counts. Track actual token usage, retries, storage, delivery charges, and review minutes by mandate. Reserve expensive reasoning for conflicting evidence; ordinary date comparisons, fee calculations, and completeness checks belong in deterministic code. Set per-mandate spend alerts and maximum retry counts. If model service disappears, continue matching from verified structured fields and issue manually reviewed deficiency requests rather than interrupting an otherwise valid closing.

Reconcile every growth forecast to retained transaction commissions. The Conservative case is $100,000 revenue less $75,000 total costs, yielding $25,000 owner profit at 25% with 1 FT + 3 C. The Base case is $550,000 revenue less $343,750 total costs, yielding $206,250 at 37.5% with the same team. The Scaled case is $1,000,000 revenue less $500,000 total costs, yielding $500,000 at 50% with 2 FT + 4 C. Illustrative fee-equivalent bridges are four closings at $25,000, eleven at $50,000, and twenty at $50,000 respectively; actual mandates can produce a different mix with identical annual retained revenue. Do not add these examples to the canonical totals. The $3,000 to $18,000 monthly opex planning range is not a substitute for each scenario's complete annual cost budget, which must include variable delivery and contractor costs. Startup capital remains $15,000 to $100,000 and first-deal timing remains 3 to 12 months. Maintain a rolling cash forecast that excludes unsigned commissions and models delayed or failed closings. Add personnel only when review queues and executable mandates justify capacity, not because the top of the funnel looks busy.

chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #26, High-Ticket Brokerage, ranks #10 with an 88/100 Money-to-Manpower Score across 21 mapped plays. Build its four-person pod around one accountable principal and three bounded contractor seats, then add execution leadership and sector analysis only when collected commissions support six people. The canonical annual owner profit cases are $25,000 Conservative, $206,250 Base, and $500,000 Scaled; underlying asset prices never enter operator revenue. This chapter turns exclusive mandates, buyer matching, diligence, NCNDA controls, and escrow closings into measurable handoffs. Weekly evidence reviews, concentration limits, signed IP assignments, and reconciled accrual cohorts create transferable operating records. Value the resulting business on defensible earnings after replacement labor, not on pipeline headlines or an unsupported premium multiple.
